title: CDL Hazmat driving, parking and training practice questions
description: Free CDL Hazmat practice questions on attending, parking, tires, routing and training rules in 49 CFR 397 and 172 Subpart H, each linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 397.1(a), the rules in Part 397 apply to a motor carrier transporting hazardous materials by a motor vehicle that meets which condition?

options.A: It has a gross vehicle weight rating of more than 26,000 pounds
options.B: It crosses a State line during the trip
options.C: It must be marked or placarded in accordance with 177.823
options.D: It is operated by a driver who holds a hazardous materials endorsement

questions.explanation: Part 397 applies "to each motor carrier engaged in the transportation of hazardous materials by a motor vehicle which must be marked or placarded in accordance with § 177.823 of this title".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.1, Application of the rules in this part (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The rules in this part apply to each motor carrier engaged in the transportation of hazardous materials by a motor vehicle which must be marked or placarded in accordance with § 177.823 of this title

questions.question: Under 397.3, a vehicle containing hazardous materials must be driven and parked in compliance with the laws, ordinances and regulations of the jurisdiction where it is operated, unless those laws are what?

options.A: At variance with specific DOT regulations that apply to the vehicle's operation and impose a more stringent obligation or restraint
options.B: Not posted on signs along the route
options.C: Adopted after the vehicle's trip began
options.D: In conflict with the motor carrier's own written policy

questions.explanation: Local laws apply "unless they are at variance with specific regulations of the Department of Transportation which are applicable to the operation of that vehicle and which impose a more stringent obligation or restraint."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.3, State and local laws, ordinances, and regulations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: unless they are at variance with specific regulations of the Department of Transportation which are applicable to the operation of that vehicle and which impose a more stringent obligation or restraint.

questions.question: A vehicle carrying Class 3 material, and no Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 material, is stopped on the shoulder of a public highway. Under 397.5(c), when may its driver leave it unattended?

options.A: During a meal break of up to 30 minutes
options.B: Whenever it is parked more than five feet from the traveled portion of the highway
options.C: Whenever the cab doors are locked
options.D: While performing duties which are incident and necessary to the driver's duties as the operator of the vehicle

questions.explanation: Such a vehicle "must be attended by its driver. However, the vehicle need not be attended while its driver is performing duties which are incident and necessary to the driver's duties as the operator of the vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: However, the vehicle need not be attended while its driver is performing duties which are incident and necessary to the driver's duties as the operator of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which situation meets the 397.5(d)(1) definition of an attended motor vehicle?

options.A: The person in charge is asleep in the sleeper berth
options.B: The person in charge is 80 feet from the vehicle and has it within an unobstructed field of view
options.C: The person in charge is 50 feet away inside a building, with the vehicle out of sight
options.D: The person in charge is 150 feet away with a clear view of the vehicle

questions.explanation: "A motor vehicle is attended when the person in charge of the vehicle is on the vehicle, awake, and not in a sleeper berth, or is within 100 feet of the vehicle and has it within his/her unobstructed field of view."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A motor vehicle is attended when the person in charge of the vehicle is on the vehicle, awake, and not in a sleeper berth, or is within 100 feet of the vehicle and has it within his/her unobstructed field of view.

questions.question: Under 397.5(d)(2), which is one of the conditions a person must meet to be a qualified representative of a motor carrier who may attend a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 material?

options.A: Is an employee of the shipper or consignee
options.B: Is authorized to move the vehicle and has the means and ability to do so
options.C: Has worked for the carrier for at least one year
options.D: Is a sworn law enforcement officer

questions.explanation: Among the listed conditions, a qualified representative "Is authorized to move the vehicle and has the means and ability to do so." The person must also have been designated by the carrier, be aware of the nature of the hazardous materials and have been instructed in emergency procedures.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Is authorized to move the vehicle and has the means and ability to do so.

questions.question: What does 397.7(a)(2) require before a vehicle containing Division 1.2 material is parked on private property, including the premises of a fueling or eating facility?

options.A: Written approval from the local fire department
options.B: A safe haven designation for the property
options.C: Notice to the shipper of the explosives
options.D: The knowledge and consent of the person in charge of the property, who is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials

questions.explanation: Such a vehicle must not be parked "On private property (including premises of fueling or eating facility) without the knowledge and consent of the person who is in charge of the property and who is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials the vehicle contains".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.7, Parking (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On private property (including premises of fueling or eating facility) without the knowledge and consent of the person who is in charge of the property and who is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials the vehicle contains

questions.question: A vehicle contains Class 8 material and no Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 material. Under 397.7(b), when may it be parked on or within five feet of the traveled portion of a public street or highway?

options.A: For brief periods when the necessities of operation require it to be parked there and make it impracticable to park it in any other place
options.B: Whenever the driver stays on the vehicle and awake
options.C: Whenever warning devices have been placed around the vehicle
options.D: Whenever it is at least 300 feet from a bridge or tunnel

questions.explanation: Such a vehicle must not be parked there "except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require the vehicle to be parked and make it impracticable to park the vehicle in any other place."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.7, Parking (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must not be parked on or within five feet of the traveled portion of public street or highway except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require the vehicle to be parked and make it impracticable to park the vehicle in any other place.

questions.question: Under 397.11(a), what must a driver do before operating a vehicle containing hazardous materials near an open fire?

options.A: Notify the local fire department
options.B: Wait until the fire is at least 300 feet from the road
options.C: Take precautions to ascertain that the vehicle can safely pass the fire without stopping
options.D: Get permission from the motor carrier's dispatcher

questions.explanation: The vehicle "must not be operated near an open fire unless its driver has first taken precautions to ascertain that the vehicle can safely pass the fire without stopping."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.11, Fires (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A motor vehicle containing hazardous materials must not be operated near an open fire unless its driver has first taken precautions to ascertain that the vehicle can safely pass the fire without stopping.

questions.question: When does the 397.13 smoking ban cover an empty tank motor vehicle?

options.A: Never; it covers only vehicles that contain hazardous materials
options.B: Whenever the empty tank still displays placards
options.C: Whenever the tank last carried any hazardous material, regardless of class
options.D: When it has been used to transport Class 3, flammable materials, or Division 2.1 flammable gases and, when so used, was required to be marked or placarded under 177.823

questions.explanation: The ban covers "An empty tank motor vehicle which has been used to transport Class 3, flammable materials, or Division 2.1 flammable gases, which when so used, was required to be marked or placarded in accordance with the rules in § 177.823 of this title."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.13, Smoking (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: An empty tank motor vehicle which has been used to transport Class 3, flammable materials, or Division 2.1 flammable gases, which when so used, was required to be marked or placarded in accordance with the rules in § 177.823 of this title.

questions.question: Under 397.17(a), when must a driver examine each tire on a motor vehicle?

options.A: At the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked
options.B: Every 2 hours or 100 miles of driving, whichever comes first
options.C: Only at the start of each duty day
options.D: Once every 24 hours of operation

questions.explanation: "A driver must examine each tire on a motor vehicle at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.17, Tires (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A driver must examine each tire on a motor vehicle at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked.

questions.question: A driver finds that a tire is overheated. What does 397.17(c) require?

options.A: Drive to the nearest safe place, then let the tire cool before continuing
options.B: Immediately cause the tire to be removed and placed at a safe distance from the vehicle, and not operate the vehicle until the cause of the overheating is corrected
options.C: Reduce speed and check the tire again at the next stop
options.D: Report the tire to the motor carrier and continue to the destination

questions.explanation: "The driver shall immediately cause the overheated tire to be removed and placed at a safe distance from the vehicle. The driver shall not operate the vehicle until the cause of the overheating is corrected." The drive to "the nearest safe place" in 397.17(b) is for flat, leaking or improperly inflated tires.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.17, Tires (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the driver shall immediately cause the overheated tire to be removed and placed at a safe distance from the vehicle. The driver shall not operate the vehicle until the cause of the overheating is corrected.

questions.question: A driver receives the documents a motor carrier must furnish under 397.19(a) for a Division 1.1 shipment. What does 397.19(b) require?

options.A: The shipper keeps a copy of the documents for two years
options.B: The driver keeps the documents in the cab for one year
options.C: The driver signs a receipt, and the motor carrier keeps the receipt for one year from the date of signature
options.D: The motor carrier files the documents with FMCSA before departure

questions.explanation: The driver "must sign a receipt for them. The motor carrier shall maintain the receipt for a period of one year from the date of signature."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.19, Instructions and documents (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A driver who receives documents in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section must sign a receipt for them. The motor carrier shall maintain the receipt for a period of one year from the date of signature.

questions.question: Under 397.19(c), the driver of a vehicle containing Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 materials must be in possession of, be familiar with, and be in compliance with which of these?

options.A: The vehicle's registration renewal notice
options.B: A permit from each State on the route
options.C: The written route plan specified in 397.67
options.D: A letter of approval from the local fire marshal

questions.explanation: The driver "must be in possession of, be familiar with, and be in compliance with" the documents in 397.19(a), the documents in 177.817, and "The written route plan specified in § 397.67."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.19, Instructions and documents (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The written route plan specified in § 397.67.

questions.question: A placarded load is not subject to any NRHM routing designation. Which situation is listed in 397.67(b) as an exception to the rule against routes through or near heavily populated areas?

options.A: A law enforcement official requires the driver to take an alternative route
options.B: The route through the city saves the driver time
options.C: The shipper asks for the fastest possible delivery
options.D: The driver knows the city streets well

questions.explanation: One listed exception is that "a situation exists where a law enforcement official requires the driver to take an alternative route." "Operating convenience is not a basis for determining whether it is practicable" to follow the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.67, Motor carrier responsibility for routing (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: a situation exists where a law enforcement official requires the driver to take an alternative route.

questions.question: A driver transports a package of highway route controlled quantity of Class 7 (radioactive) materials. Under 397.101(e)(2), where must the driver's certificate of training be?

options.A: On file with the shipper only
options.B: Posted inside the cab next to the shipping papers
options.C: Kept at the carrier's terminal, available on request
options.D: In the driver's immediate possession, with a copy placed in the driver's qualification file

questions.explanation: "The driver has in his or her immediate possession a certificate of training as evidence of training required by this section, and a copy is placed in his or her qualification file".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.101, Requirements for motor carriers and drivers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The driver has in his or her immediate possession a certificate of training as evidence of training required by this section, and a copy is placed in his or her qualification file

questions.question: How does the 171.8 definition of hazmat employee treat a self-employed owner-operator of a motor vehicle?

options.A: It excludes them; only persons employed by a hazmat employer are hazmat employees
options.B: It includes them when they transport hazardous materials in commerce and, in the course of that self-employment, directly affect hazardous materials transportation safety
options.C: It includes them only if they hold a hazardous materials endorsement
options.D: It includes them only if they employ at least one other driver

questions.explanation: A hazmat employee includes a person who is "Self-employed (including an owner-operator of a motor vehicle, vessel, or aircraft) transporting hazardous materials in commerce who in the course of such self-employment directly affects hazardous materials transportation safety".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Self-employed (including an owner-operator of a motor vehicle, vessel, or aircraft) transporting hazardous materials in commerce who in the course of such self-employment directly affects hazardous materials transportation safety

questions.question: Under 172.701, a State may impose more stringent training requirements for motor vehicle drivers only if those requirements do not conflict with Subpart H and Part 177 and meet which other condition?

options.A: They apply only to drivers domiciled in that State
options.B: They apply to every driver who enters the State
options.C: They are approved by each neighboring State
options.D: They replace the federal three-year recurrent training cycle

questions.explanation: "For motor vehicle drivers, however, a State may impose more stringent training requirements only if those requirements" do not conflict and "Apply only to drivers domiciled in that State."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.701, Federal-State relationship (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Apply only to drivers domiciled in that State.

questions.question: Under 172.704(c)(1), a new hazmat employee may perform hazmat functions before completing training if the training is completed within 90 days after employment and which other condition is met?

options.A: The employee has read the carrier's safety manual
options.B: The employee holds a hazardous materials endorsement
options.C: The employer has notified FMCSA of the new hire
options.D: The employee performs those functions under the direct supervision of a properly trained and knowledgeable hazmat employee

questions.explanation: The employee may perform those functions provided "The employee performs those functions under the direct supervision of a properly trained and knowledgeable hazmat employee" and "The training is completed within 90 days after employment or a change in job function."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.704, Training requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employee performs those functions under the direct supervision of a properly trained and knowledgeable hazmat employee

questions.question: Under 172.704(c)(3), when may relevant training a driver received from a previous employer be used to satisfy Subpart H?

options.A: Only if it was given in the same State
options.B: Whenever the driver states that it covered the same subjects
options.C: Provided a current record of training is obtained from the hazmat employee's previous employer
options.D: Only if it was completed within the past 12 months

questions.explanation: "Relevant training received from a previous employer or other source may be used to satisfy the requirements of this subpart provided a current record of training is obtained from hazmat employees' previous employer."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.704, Training requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Relevant training received from a previous employer or other source may be used to satisfy the requirements of this subpart provided a current record of training is obtained from hazmat employees' previous employer.

questions.question: Which item does 172.704(d) list as part of the record of current training a hazmat employer must keep?

options.A: The employee's home address
options.B: The name and address of the person providing the training
options.C: The employee's score on each test question
options.D: The employee's date of birth

questions.explanation: "The record must include" the employee's name, the most recent completion date, the training materials, "The name and address of the person providing the training" and certification that the employee "has been trained and tested".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.704, Training requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The name and address of the person providing the training
